rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest calls, both resolve: chunk 2 line 14 'today you step away' and chunk 2 line 16 'this module's un-watched session' lean on 'session' established in chunk 0 title + chunk 1 Big Idea ('Prep your first long session'). Chunk 8 line 70 'They all point at the same surprise' precedes its antecedent (the four reading items) but within the SAME chunk, immediately below — same-chunk forward reference to enumerated list content directly following, not a violation of the ban on pointing at a LATER slide.

Chunk 2 line 14 names the source by title ('Simon Willison's Designing agentic loops') and unpacks its claim in the same sentence ('it names the thinking you do before stepping away'), not by file position. Line 16 names 'Horthy's Why Software Factories Fail' by title, same pattern, newly-added inline attribution this session. Both pass the navigational-pointer carve-out (named, not located).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 4 line 27 'a bug fix, a plan read' — grep confirmed a bug-fix beat exists (getting-going.md Ex2 'fix-tests-first', the M1 TDD exercise) and a plan-read beat exists (plan-mode-done-right.md, the M3 module whose whole arc is reading/critiquing plan-mode output). Neither is a dangling reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body; this rule has nothing to bind to in a module file that only lists links and framing prose.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or a nameable list (e.g. chunk 7 'Bring to Module 5' states the artefact requirement and the risk of arriving without one in two sentences); none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked each header against its chunk body: 'Start here' (chunk 4) opens with orientation + the room's opening question + the reading/exercise list, true to 'start here'; 'Bring to Module 5' (chunk 7) states exactly what to bring; 'Pre-reads before Module 5' (chunk 8) is an optional reading list. No header contradicted by its own content.

Scanned every chunk for the five sub-items: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative (grepped 'one of the' / 'most useful' etc — zero hits in body); no number-with-retraction; no abstraction-noun stack; no verb triplet with an empty leg. Closest-to-tic line is chunk 4 line 29's list of six task types (migration, gnarly refactor, ...) — that is a plain enumeration, not a cadence pattern, and stays clear.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'surface|compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections' over lines 1-83 (body only) returns zero hits; every hit the same grep returns over the full file lands at or after line 86, inside the maintainer block, out of body scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Per-chunk bold count: chunk 2 (Prework) carries one bolded sentence at line 10 ('A real slice you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than a big epic.') — this is a task-size floor-and-ceiling statement sitting in a `## Prework` section, matching the §34/§9 exception verbatim ('a bolded line that names a task-size floor and ceiling, sitting in ## Prework, ## Bring to Module N, or ## Next') — N/A by the rule's own carve-out, not a count violation. Chunk 3 (What You'll Learn) bolds one verb per LO bullet (Scope/Walk/Fill/Send off) — the module-shape LO template exception, also N/A. Chunk 4 (Start here) — the flagged item: line 29 '**The question, to you:**' is the ONLY bold element in that chunk, ≲5 words, a colon-terminated label distinguishing the pivot question from the surrounding orientation prose, not a decorated whole-lead-sentence. It reads closer to the cleared '**Read:**/**Watch:**' mode-marker function (marking 'this is the one thing to answer' the way a mode word marks 'this is how to engage') than to the banned pre-2026-07-09 monoculture (every bullet opening bolded). Budget of ≤1 per slide is met exactly, and no monoculture or clutter is present — the harm the rule guards against is absent. Closest-call ruling: PASS, on the strength of (a) single bold, well under budget, (b) handle-length span, not a sentence, (c) functions as a navigational pivot-marker, the same spirit as the cleared mode-word carve-out, even though 'the question, to you' does not literally name a law/governor/coined term. If a future judge wants a bright line instead of a functional read, the rule would need a fifth handle category ('a pivot label introducing the slide's single load-bearing question') to make this an uncontestable PASS rather than a judgment call. Chunk 8 (Pre-reads) bolds 'Read,' / 'Watch,' / 'Read,' / 'Read (longer),' per entry — exact match to the reading-list/menu carve-out (mode word bolded, title left plain), budget-off there by design. No other chunk carries bold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
